scope: Research informing the comparison-first quiz design. These studies do not validate Art Atlas or its profile families.

references.title: Just Sort It! A Simple and Effective Approach to Active Preference Learning
references.researchSetting: Adaptive pair comparisons and ranking under probabilistic comparison models.
references.findingUsed: Choosing comparisons strategically can recover rankings with fewer comparisons than indiscriminate sampling.
references.application: Use a small number of cross-group comparisons to resolve uncertain relationships among previously seen paintings. Keep the identities, original questions and order evidence attached to each comparison.
references.boundary: The paper does not establish a uniquely correct art preference model, explain psychological causes, or validate our current selection heuristic. Separate groups cannot supply a global observed ranking until comparison paths connect them.

references.title: Time after time, the best–worst scaling method is more reliable than ranking
references.authors: Garston Liang, Mackenzie Glover and Guy E. Hawkins
references.researchSetting: Three experiments comparing ranking and best–worst choices for life values.
references.findingUsed: Best–worst choices produced stronger test–retest reliability than rankings in the studied setting.
references.application: Small sets and easy extreme choices motivate reducing demands for absolute 0–100 judgements. Separate explicit favourite and dislike selections from the relative ordering of a group.
references.boundary: Our granular line with optional ties is not a balanced best–worst scaling experiment. The study did not test paintings. We cannot claim its reliability estimates, treat a set winner as liked, or treat a set loser as disliked.

references.title: How Stable Are Human Aesthetic Preferences Across the Lifespan?
references.authors: Cameron Pugach, Helmut Leder and Daniel J. Graham
references.researchSetting: Repeated rank-order judgements of paintings and other visual stimuli over two weeks.
references.findingUsed: Art preferences showed changes between sessions. Stability cannot be assumed from a single response.
references.application: Repeat a few exact comparisons after a delay and show changes as observed choices, without interpreting them as personal unreliability. Keep repeat responses separate from independent evidence for a pattern.
references.boundary: A changed order does not identify its cause. Context, attention, familiarity and changing responses remain possible explanations. Within-session repeats do not establish long-term stability.

references.title: Ratings or pairwise comparisons? An experimental study on scale usability
references.researchSetting: Ratings and pair comparisons of physical object dimensions against known measurements.
references.findingUsed: Both approaches could represent the measured physical characteristics in this experiment.
references.application: Keep directly reported responses as useful evidence, while making the task and scale explicit. Do not assume that comparison tasks universally dominate rating tasks.
references.boundary: The stimuli had measurable physical dimensions. There is no corresponding objective ground-truth score for how much someone should like a painting.

implementationRules: For the new relative comparison instrument, point placement supplies order and exact ties. Point gaps are not confidence, intensity of liking, or cross-group utility.
Earlier overall-rating and legacy comparison records keep their original instrument identity and are never silently converted.
Explicit favourites and dislikes, admiration, symbolic interpretation, recognition, emotional responses and curatorial grouping remain separate observations.
A proposed pattern needs contrasts, independent works and counterexamples. Shared artist, period or movement is not a psychological explanation.
A held-out prediction must be recorded before the answer and assessed without training on that answer. Repeats and adaptive checks are not extra independent discovery sets.
evaluationRequired: Pilot the relative line against direct pair choices using completion effort, exact-repeat agreement and held-out choice accuracy.
Measure whether profile explanations remain useful when artwork identity and correlated qualities are controlled.
Record support and failures. Do not publish population rarity, personality scores or calibrated confidence without appropriate validation data.
